subject: physiology
title: Adrenal cortex and medulla

steps.tx: The **adrenal cortex** stacks three zones from outside in: glomerulosa makes aldosterone, fasciculata makes cortisol and is widest, and reticularis makes dehydroepiandrosterone and androgens. Cholesterol reaches mitochondria on the StAR protein, adrenocorticotropic hormone drives cortisol and androgens, and angiotensin drives aldosterone, remembered as glomerulosa, fasciculata, reticularis. Inside sits the medulla of chromaffin cells making adrenaline and noradrenaline for fight or flight, and failure of cortex in Addison disease darkens skin.
steps.say: From capsule inward the cortex lays down salt, sugar and sex steroids in that order, and the innermost medulla stores catecholamines. The glomerulosa secretes aldosterone under angiotensin control, the fasciculata secretes cortisol under pituitary control, and the reticularis secretes androgens. Cholesterol delivery by StAR is beginning every steroid, while splanchnic nerves are firing the medulla in stress. When the whole cortex fails, pigmentation deepens in Addison disease.

vis.alt: Layers of the adrenal gland from outside in: capsule, zona glomerulosa making aldosterone, zona fasciculata making cortisol, zona reticularis making androgens, and the medulla making adrenaline and noradrenaline.
vis.caption: Salt, sugar, sex from outside in: glomerulosa aldosterone, fasciculata cortisol, reticularis androgens, medulla catecholamines.

steps.tx: **Aldosterone** follows renin from juxtaglomerular cells when perfusion falls: angiotensin converting enzyme makes angiotensin II, which constricts vessels at AT1 receptors and releases aldosterone, while high potassium directly triggers release. Aldosterone retains sodium and water follows, Conn adenoma causes hypertension with low potassium, and spironolactone blocks the receptor while eplerenone spares gynaecomastia. Antidiuretic hormone and thirst balance water, angiotensin inhibitors lower the drive, and liquorice glycyrrhizin mimics aldosterone excess.
steps.say: Renin starts the cascade when the kidney senses low pressure or low sodium, and angiotensin II then squeezes vessels and calls for aldosterone, as the flow diagram shows. Aldosterone keeps sodium and water and wastes potassium, so an autonomous adenoma in Conn syndrome raises pressure while potassium falls. Spironolactone blocks the receptor, eplerenone avoids breast tenderness, and liquorice can imitate the whole picture.

vis.alt: Flow diagram of the renin angiotensin aldosterone system: low renal perfusion or low sodium at the macula densa or sympathetic activity releases renin, which converts angiotensinogen to angiotensin I, ACE converts it to angiotensin II, which constricts vessels and drives aldosterone, retaining sodium and water.
vis.caption: Renin, ACE, AT1: angiotensin II constricts vessels and releases aldosterone, which keeps sodium and water and wastes potassium.

steps.tx: **Cortisol** rises in stress such as surgery and sepsis, drives gluconeogenesis and diabetes, suppresses immunity and vaccines, thins bone toward osteoporosis and avascular necrosis, and in excess gives Cushing features of moon face, striae and buffalo hump with central weight. Dexamethasone suppression fails in ectopic disease, metyrapone blocks eleven beta hydroxylation, and steroids must taper lest the axis crash. Levels peak in the morning and trough at midnight, shift work flattens the rhythm, and inhaled or skin steroids still absorb.
steps.say: Cortisol is the stress steroid: it raises glucose, dampens immunity, and thins bone, peaking early in the morning and falling to a midnight trough. Too much produces the moon face, purple striae and central obesity of Cushing syndrome, while suppression tests and the blocker metyrapone help locate the source, tracing the pituitary adrenal loop in the diagram. Never stop long term steroids suddenly, because the suppressed axis needs time to wake.

vis.alt: Hypothalamic pituitary adrenal axis: stress releases CRH from the hypothalamus, which releases ACTH from the anterior pituitary, which stimulates cortisol from the zona fasciculata; cortisol feeds back negatively on both CRH and ACTH.
vis.caption: Stress to CRH to ACTH to cortisol, with cortisol shutting off its own drive; steroid therapy suppresses the axis.

steps.tx: The medulla builds **catecholamines** from tyrosine through DOPA and dopamine to noradrenaline and adrenaline: adrenaline gives beta effects of sweating and tremor, noradrenaline gives alpha pressor effects. Phaeochromocytoma breaks the ten percent rule with paroxysms, found by MIBG scanning and urinary metanephrines, needing alpha blockade with phenoxybenzamine before laparoscopic surgery lest unopposed beta stimulation kill. Reticularis dehydroepiandrosterone brings adrenarche and pubic hair, twenty one hydroxylase deficiency virilises and wastes salt, hirsutism uses Ferriman scoring, and neonatal haemorrhage follows anoxia.
steps.say: Adrenaline and noradrenaline come from tyrosine in steps, with the cortisol dependent last step explaining why adrenaline is mainly adrenal, as the synthesis figure shows. A phaeochromocytoma causes paroxysmal headaches, sweating and palpitations, confirmed by metanephrines and MIBG scanning, and alpha blockade must precede surgery. Nearby androgen problems include adrenarche from dehydroepiandrosterone, virilising congenital adrenal hyperplasia, and hirsutism scored at the bedside.

vis.alt: Catecholamine synthesis in order: tyrosine to L-DOPA by tyrosine hydroxylase, the rate limiting step, then to dopamine, noradrenaline, and adrenaline by PNMT, which is induced by cortisol.
vis.caption: Tyrosine hydroxylase is rate limiting; PNMT needs cortisol, so adrenaline is made mainly in the adrenal medulla.
